after.guide:
How to play:
1. Press “Import into Minecraft” or double-click {output} to import it into Minecraft.
2. Create a new world and activate this add-on under both Behavior Packs and Resource Packs (a superflat world works best).
3. Enter the world and type these commands in chat:
{commands}
4. Use a compass to open the remote (play, pause, switch videos).
web.subtitle: Web Converter (beta)
web.intro: Turn videos into a Minecraft Bedrock add-on (.mcaddon) entirely in your browser. Your videos are never uploaded.
web.vox_hint: MagicaVoxel animations (.vox) can be added too: their size and frames are kept, and only FPS and palette apply.
web.memory_warning: Long for the browser: the frames take about {mb} MB of memory. If the page stops, shorten the length, lower the size or fps, or use the Windows app.
web.howto_import: Open the .mcaddon to import it into Minecraft. In the world settings, turn on both the behavior pack and the resource pack (cheats are not needed).
web.howto_import_legacy: Open the .mcaddon to import it into Minecraft. In the world settings, turn on both the behavior pack and the resource pack, and turn cheats on (this older-version add-on is controlled with /scriptevent).
web.howto_setup: On flat ground, run {setup} and then {start}. Use a compass to open the remote control.
web.howto_note: The first time, the page loads Python for the converter (about 20 MB), which takes a while. The browser version converts on the CPU only, so for long videos or large screens the Windows app (with GPU support) is faster.
web.load_estimate: Playback load estimate: {blocks} blocks/s when the whole picture changes ({level})

web.audio_aac: Decoding the AAC track taken out of the video

web.usage_note: To learn how many people use it, this page counts with GoatCounter: page opens (with the display language), and add-on builds started, finished and failed (for finished ones, the kind of add-on and the display language). Only these counts are sent: no cookies, no file names and no videos.
web.preview_note: How the add-on looks in Minecraft, drawn with the same rules as the game (3D is seen from above at an angle). Check it before you import.

web.hero_title: Turn any video into Minecraft blocks
web.drop_title: Drop videos, pictures or .vox files here
web.tip_preset: Sets width, height and FPS together. Bigger and smoother looks better but places more blocks every second.
web.tip_size: Size of the screen in blocks (one block per pixel). Use “Match video aspect ratio” to avoid black bars.
web.tip_fps: Frames per second in Minecraft, up to 20 (the game's tick rate). Higher is smoother but heavier.
web.tip_duration: Seconds from the start to convert. Leave it empty to convert the whole video.
web.tip_mode: A flat screen, or a 3D sculpture shaped by the brightness of the picture.
web.tip_depth: How many blocks deep the 3D modes can go.
web.tip_palette: Which blocks can be used. Auto picks the colours that suit each scene.
web.tip_dither: Mixes neighbouring blocks to show colours the palette does not have. None gives flat areas with clean edges.
web.tip_image: Also makes a separate add-on that shows the video as pictures instead of blocks. Not yet checked in Minecraft.
web.tip_keyframe: How often a whole frame is stored. Shorter makes seeking recover sooner, longer makes the add-on smaller. 0 = only at the start of each group.
web.tip_target: 1.26.10 or newer has its own commands. For 1.21.80 to 1.26.0 the commands go through /scriptevent, so cheats must be on.
web.tip_namespace: Commands start with this, for example /badapple:start. Lowercase letters, numbers and _ only.
web.stage_caption: The right half is real output from this converter at its default settings (128 × 72 blocks, 10 fps, auto palette, Blue Noise), decoded by the same code the add-on runs in the game.
web.showcase_lead: Pick a size, a palette and a dithering method. Every picture is real output from this converter for one frame of the sample.
web.showcase_readout: {blocks} blocks, {colours} block colours in this frame
web.inputs_title: Four kinds of input, one add-on
web.inputs_lead: Everything is converted in this browser tab and packed into a .mcaddon file for Minecraft Bedrock.
web.pipe_browser_note: Python running as WebAssembly. Nothing is uploaded.
web.pipe_addon_note: Behavior pack and resource pack in one file
web.how_title: From file to world in four steps
web.how_1_text: Drop videos, pictures or .vox files, record with the camera, or pick an MMD model and dance.
web.how_2_text: Start from a quality preset, then adjust size, frame rate, palette and dithering if you want.
web.how_3_text: The page reads the frames, converts them and packs the add-on. A preview shows how it will look in the game.
web.privacy_lead: The conversion runs in this tab. Here is exactly what moves over the network and what does not.
web.privacy_stays_2: Every frame and the sound taken from them
web.privacy_stays_3: The finished add-on: it is made in memory and saved by your browser
web.privacy_loads_2: The converter itself: Python for the browser, about 30 MB on the first visit, from this site (a fixed, checked version; nothing is loaded from other sites)
web.convert_lead: Add files, adjust the settings and build. The add-on is saved straight from this tab.
web.footer_disclaimer: Not an official Minecraft product. Not approved by or associated with Mojang or Microsoft.
